episodes.title: The Room of Pictures: Ezekiel 4-8, Job 2, John 7, 2 Peter 1
episodes.summary: Ezekiel 4-8 was taught as the mute prophet's sign-acts and the first temple vision (593-592 B.C., Zedekiah reigning, 8:1 dated the sixth year, sixth month, fifth day). The brick siege drew Calvin's 'childish spectacle, unless God had commanded' and Henry's contrast with Zion on God's palms. The 390 and 40 days (nasa avon) were explained as Jeroboam to the fall plus Judah's last forty years (Calvin, Henry), with Keil's 430 as a new Egypt and Poole's 'God in very deed had patiently borne with them'. The hard question, whether Ezekiel literally lay there, set Calvin (vision only) and Keil's arithmetic (413 versus 437 days) against Henry (real, at set hours); the host sided with Henry. The one New Testament move: Ezekiel displays the burden while Isaiah 53:12 and 1 Peter 2:24 show the one who bears it away (Calvin and Keil: no expiation here). Also covered: the dung bread and Ezekiel's 'Ah, Lord God' as pleading within obedience; the razor and the sifted remnant (Poole); 'This is Jerusalem' at the center of the nations; 6:9 nishbarti 'I have been broken' (Henry's grieved husband, Calvin's two senses); qets and Amos 8:2; and 7:10 'the rod has blossomed' set against Aaron's rod (Calvin: the seed of the staff was their pride). In chapter 8 the four scenes were the image of jealousy (Manasseh's Asherah); the seventy elders in the room of pictures (maskit) with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan, set against Shaphan's godly sons in Jeremiah (Ahikam, Gemariah, Elasah, Gedaliah); 'The Lord does not see us' as complaint not theory (Calvin); Tammuz, the month of 1:1, with Jerome's Bethlehem grove of Adonis (Letter 58); the twenty-five sun-worshipers with backs to the temple, with Mishnah Sukkah 5:4 ('and we, our eyes are to God'); and the branch to the nose left open. Application: let God dig into the hidden room and build a chamber of devotion (Henry paraphrased). Job 2 covered the second council, tummah, hinnam turned back on Satan (Gill, Poole), Gregory on God being 'moved', skin for skin, Deuteronomy 28:35, mud with mud, the wife quoting God's words with Satan's conclusion (Gregory quoted; Spurgeon 3255 gentler, paraphrased), nabal, Henry on good and evil 'from the hand of God', lips versus heart, Teman and Shuah, and the seven days of silence as the friends' best moment. John 7:45-53 covered the officers (Chrysostom 'came back bound themselves by wonder'; Spurgeon 951 'he had fairly taken them'; Calvin 'softened rather than broken' paraphrased), the Pharisees' contempt, Nicodemus (Calvin severe, Augustine kind, Calvin's hidden seed and John 19:39), Jonah of Gath-hepher, Isaiah 9 and Augustine's 'Yet the Lord of the prophets arose thence', and the 7:53-8:11 text question deferred. 2 Peter 1:12-21 covered esterigmenous and sterizo, skenoma and exodos echoing the Transfiguration (Luke 9:31), Calvin's last words as a testament, Piper (1982) 'the difference ... is history', the 'more sure' question (Calvin; Reformation Study Bible; Piper and the ESV, which the host took), auchmeros as squalid, Calvin and Augustine on the day as the last day, William Bridge's 'the more you will lift up your hands and admire', 1:20 as origin not reader, pheromenoi with the voice 'borne' and the ship of Acts 27 (Barnes), and Westminster Confession 1.10. Closing connections: the dark painted room (Ezekiel 8) and the lamp in a squalid place (2 Peter 1:19); the Booths reversal of Ezekiel 8:16 and the officers at that same feast.
threads: Ezekiel 9-12 is next: the man clothed in linen with the writing case marks foreheads of those who sigh and groan (9:4; check whether Cyprian or other fathers read the tav mark as the cross before quoting), judgment beginning at the sanctuary (9:6, already tied to 1 Peter 4:17 in episode 11), the glory moving to the threshold (9:3, 10:4) and leaving to the mountain east of the city (11:23), the cherubim identified (10:20), Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah (11:1, 13; Keil distinguishes him from 8:11's son of Shaphan), the 'new heart' promise (11:19), and Ezekiel's baggage sign and covered face (12). Calvin's lectures continue through chapter 20.
The muteness thread (3:26 until 33:22) and the glory arc (1-3 arrives, 8-11 departs, 43 returns, 48:35) continue. Today the glory was still present at 8:4 but 'driven far' (8:6).

Unused Ezekiel 4-8 material: Calvin's prayers at the end of Lectures 11 and 17; Calvin on the iron pan and sacraments needing God's word; Henry's 'fancy is like fire, a good servant, but a bad master', 'Oh that the wickedness of the wicked might come to an end, before it bring them to an end!', 'serve an idol in tears', and 'some hole or other left in the wall'; Gregory the Great's Pastoral Rule on 8:8 ('what is digging in a wall but opening the hardness of the heart by sharp inquisitions?'); Poole on the backs to the temple as 'abrenunciation'; Ligonier 'Learning God's Lessons' on post-exilic monotheism; Gill on the navel of the earth.

Job 3 is next: Job curses the day of his birth, the first poetry of the book, and the first speech after seven days of silence. Henry's 'They were silent, as men astonished and amazed' and Spurgeon 3255's 'Their tender mercies were cruel, though well-intentioned' are unused. Gregory's Moralia Book IV covers Job 3. Unused Job 2: Tertullian's 'How did God smile' (Of Patience 14), Gregory's 'the old enemy was beaten by Adam on a dunghill, he that conquered Adam in Paradise', Gill on Job's wife as normally good.

John 8:1-11 is next: the pericope adulterae and its absence from the earliest manuscripts (the ESV brackets 7:53-8:11); state the Presbyterian and confessional approach to textual criticism briefly (Westminster Confession 1.8) and teach the passage honestly. Augustine's Tractate 33 continues into 8:1-11 ('misery and mercy'). John 8:12 'I am the light of the world' follows, set up today by Isaiah 9:1-2 and Augustine's 'Lord of the prophets', plus the Mishnah Sukkah lamps.

2 Peter 2:1-9 is next: false prophets among the people as false teachers among you (picks up 1:19-21 directly), destructive heresies, denying the Master who bought them, angels cast into Tartarus, Noah a herald of righteousness, Lot righteous and distressed, 'the Lord knows how to rescue the godly'. Unused 2 Peter 1 material: Dever's 'You have to be pretty certain of the truth to die for it' and 'It's no insult to anyone to remind them' (Ligonier, 'Certain Truth'); Piper's 'His bequest to the church is not money' and 'dawn without and daystar within'; Calvin's 'who ruled in their mouth as in his own sanctuary' and 'their doctrine lives and prevails'; Augustine Tractate 35 on lamps.

Voices used this episode: Calvin (Ezekiel 2 quoted, many paraphrased; John and 2 Peter paraphrased), Poole, Henry (2), Jerome, the Mishnah, Gregory the Great, Chrysostom, Spurgeon (951), Augustine, Piper (SermonIndex copy of a 1982 Desiring God sermon), William Bridge, Westminster Confession 1.10; paraphrased Keil and Delitzsch, Gill, Ligonier devotionals, Spurgeon 3255, the Reformation Study Bible, Barnes, Ellicott. No Spurgeon sermon on Ezekiel 4-8 exists in the indexes checked. Desiring God still returns 403. Next time consider Cyprian on the tav mark (Ezekiel 9:4), Owen, Watson, Brooks, Boston, Ryle on John 8, Augustine Tractate 33, Schreiner or MacArthur on 2 Peter 2, and Gregory's Moralia Book IV.

episodes.title: The Mark of the Mourners: Ezekiel 9-12, Job 3, John 8, 2 Peter 2
episodes.summary: Ezekiel 9-12 was taught as the end of the 592 B.C. temple vision and the staged departure of the glory: 9:3 to the threshold, 10:18-19 to the east gate, 11:23 to the Mount of Olives, with Henry's 'God's departures from a people are gradual'. 9:4 covered the man in linen marking those who sigh and groan (ne'enachim, ne'enaqim) and the tav as a signature mark (Job 31:35). Tertullian's cross reading was set against Poole's 'too curious' and Keil's middle way (paraphrased), with Revelation 7:3 as the first New Testament move. The hard question was whether the mark spared the godly; Calvin's answer was that it means separation and God's faithfulness, not immunity from all injury. Also covered: 9:9 quoting 8:12 back at the elders; coals scattered rather than cleansing (Isaiah 6); Calvin on Psalm 132 and the interrupted promise; the cauldron slogan of 11:3 mocking Jeremiah 29, and Riblah; the irony of the names Pelatiah and Benaiah; 'men of your redemption' (11:15) with Calvin on the church in hiding places; miqdash me'at (11:16) with Spurgeon No. 2001's 'travelling temple' and Henry's temple-without-God contrast; and 11:19-20 with Calvin's stone that cannot be inscribed, 2 Corinthians 3:3 as the second New Testament move, Sproul's 'regeneration precedes faith' via Ligonier, and Westminster Confession 10. Ezekiel 12 covered the baggage sign (digging through the wall echoing 8:8) and Zedekiah 'shall not see it', with Josephus on Zedekiah disbelieving both prophets, and the two proverbs of delay (Henry paraphrased). Application: be a mourner, not a commentator. Job 3 covered the switch to poetry and the three movements, with Trapp's 'Diem, non Deum'. Qalal was set against barak, then came Genesis 1 reversed (Ash), Sheol as rest, and the hedge of 3:23 against 1:10 (Poole). The 'did Job sin' question was answered with Calvin's 'mixture' (paraphrased from his sermons) and Poole: no blasphemy, but real infirmity. The segment also covered the parallel with Jeremiah 20, a pastoral word on despair, and Derek Thomas's 'utterly honest'. John 7:53-8:11 addressed the textual question with Westminster Confession 1.8, Calvin's 'nothing unworthy of an Apostolic Spirit' and Carson (paraphrased). It then covered the trap and the missing man, the views on what Jesus wrote (Augustine, Ambrose and Jerome on Jeremiah 17:13, Calvin), Deuteronomy 17:7 with Sproul, conviction versus repentance (Calvin), Augustine's 'the wretched woman and Mercy', Henry's 'I do forgive thee', and MacArthur on the cross. 2 Peter 2:1-9 covered pareisago, plastos and emporeuomai (the Master bought them; they sell you) and 'their destruction is not asleep'. On 2:1 and definite atonement it gave Gill's 'the Father' view (Deuteronomy 32:6), then Poole's visible-church reading (quoted), Schreiner and Owen paraphrased, Westminster Confession 8.8 and Thomas Adams. It finished with the four-part 'if' and 'then' (Jude contrasted), Clement of Rome on Noah preaching repentance, and Lot as righteous through imputed righteousness, with his ongoing grief as the evidence. Closing connections: the ESV cross-reference from 2 Peter 2:8 to Ezekiel 9:4 (mourners, Lot, and the gleeful accusers of John 8), and the delay proverb of Ezekiel 12:22 answered by 2 Peter 2:3.
threads: Ezekiel 13-15 is next: false prophets who whitewash a wall (13:10-16), the women who sew magic bands, elders with idols in their hearts (14:3), Noah, Daniel and Job (14:14, 20), and the useless vine (15). Job was named today, so link Ezekiel 14:14 to the Job readings. Keep tracking the glory arc: it left to the Mount of Olives at 11:23 and returns by the east gate in 43:1-5. The muteness (3:26 until 33:22) continues. Calvin's lectures run through chapter 20.

Unused Ezekiel 9-12 material: Henry's 'Here the honours of the pen exceeded those of the sword', his note that the man in linen 'reported his matter' while the destroyers did not, 'God will set a mark upon his mourners, will book their sighs and bottle their tears', and 'Perhaps it was Ezekiel's infirmity to bewail the death of this wicked prince'. Calvin's 'For they sin doubly' (9:6), 'fell upon his face as a mediator' (9:8), 'unbelievers turn the patience of God into material for obduracy' (12:22), 'we must still go on, although success does not answer to our labor' (12:3), God as hunter with hidden nets (12:13), and the 'half of God's covenant' warning (11:19-20). Gill's rabbinic ten removes of the Shekinah (Rosh Hashanah 31a) and the Targum's synagogues reading of 11:16. Ellicott on the mark referring 'wholly and only to character'. The Pulpit Commentary naming Jeremiah, Baruch, Ahikam and Gedaliah among the marked. Spurgeon No. 2001's 'The Holy of Holies was great for holiness, but not for space'. Spurgeon's 'The Heart of Flesh' sermon is saved for Ezekiel 36:26.

Job 4 is next: Eliphaz the Temanite speaks first, the night vision (4:12-21), and 'who that was innocent ever perished?' (4:7). Unused Job 3 material: Gregory's 'closed vessels' and 'Adam was created, but Cain was the first man that was born', Trapp's 'never hath any yet been heard to curse the day of his new birth', Caryl's 'Troubles will make a man Rhetoricall' and 'Plenty of sorrow makes a scarcity of words', Ishodad of Merv on grief without blasphemy, Henry's Concise 'willing to die... willing to live', Spurgeon No. 2666's 'not with a hedge of roses, but with a barrier of briars', and Poole on 3:23. Note the qalal bookend with 40:4 'I am of small account' for when Job answers God.

John 8:12-20 is next: 'I am the light of the world' at Booths, with the Mishnah Sukkah lamps lighting every courtyard (fetched in earlier research), Isaiah 9:1-2 and Augustine's 'Lord of the prophets' from episode 15, the testimony of two witnesses, and 'in the treasury' (8:20). Unused 8:1-11 material: Ambrose Letter 26 ('in the remission of sins no man can participate with Christ'), Bengel ('He does not add, in peace'), Lightfoot's bitter-water analogy, Ryle on conscience and on the text, Sproul's 'clothed us with the cloak of His righteousness', and Augustine's account of the passage being removed from manuscripts.

2 Peter 2:10-16 is next: despising authority, blaspheming the glorious ones, 'irrational animals', 'eyes full of adultery', and Balaam's donkey. Unused 2:1-9 material: Owen's 'no purchase mentioned... but a deliverance', Adams's two arms of God and 'Just Lot was delivered, neither for his justice, nor without it', Spurgeon No. 2441's 'it is better that He should know than that we should know', Calvin's 'kept to be punished' and his note on Tartarus sobriety, 1 Clement 11 on Lot's hospitality, and Ligonier's 'Jesus buys false teachers only in that He incorporates them into the visible church'.

Voices quoted this episode: Henry (2), Tertullian, Poole (2), Calvin (3), Spurgeon (No. 2001), Josephus, Trapp, Derek Thomas, Augustine, and Clement of Rome. Paraphrased: Keil and Delitzsch, Gill, Ligonier (Sproul), Christopher Ash, Carson, MacArthur, Sproul, Ambrose, Jerome, Schreiner, Owen, Thomas Adams, and Westminster Confession 1.8, 8.8 and 10. Desiring God still returns 403, so no Piper. Next time consider Caryl, Gregory's Moralia on Job 4, Ryle and Chrysostom on John 8:12, Calvin's lectures on Ezekiel 13-14, Manton or Adams on 2 Peter 2:10-16, and Bunyan or Watson.

episodes.title: Whitewash: Ezekiel 13-15, Job 4, John 8, 2 Peter 2
episodes.summary: Ezekiel 13-15 was taught inside the 592-591 B.C. block between 8:1 and 20:1 as three answers to three false securities (our prophets say peace; we have righteous men and are consulting the prophet; we are God's vine), picking up 12:24's promise to end flattering divination. Chapter 13 covered prophets 'from their own hearts', jackals among ruins, the breach (Calvin teaching, Henry prayer, Psalm 106:23, Poole's fox-like flight), chayits (a flimsy partition wall, hapax) and tafel (whitewash, also 'tasteless' in Job 6:6 and Lamentations 2:14), Calvin's 'peace with God by becoming enemies to ourselves', Spurgeon No. 816 (1868) 'Sing men a soft song of peace', Trapp's 'popguns', Matthew 7:26-27 as New Testament move one, and the prophetesses' bands and veils for barley with Gregory the Great's cushions ('lie softly in error'). Chapter 14 covered idols taken into the heart (gillulim; Henry 'Many who have no idols in their sanctuary have idols in their hearts'), the hard question of 14:9 'I have deceived that prophet' (Calvin and Keil against mere permission, 1 Kings 22 and pittah, Henry 'Both are sins in him who does them', Westminster Confession 5.4 paraphrased), Noah, Daniel and Job (Daniel alive at court; the Ugaritic Danel view set aside; Criswell paraphrased; Keil and Jerome's ladder; Augustine on Noah's drunkenness; Spurgeon No. 1651 'No proxy in these matters is possible'), and 14:22-23 with Henry (repentant survivors) against Calvin and Keil (wicked survivors vindicate God), the host siding with Calvin. Chapter 15's useless vine wood was tied to John 15:6 as the second New Testament move. Application: before asking God for guidance, ask what answer you have already decided not to accept. Job 4 covered Eliphaz of Teman (Jeremiah 49:7), the three movements, Gregory's 'testimony ... told by him, who aims to fasten guilt', naga 'touch' as Satan's verb (Henry), Trapp's 'commend a man with a but', five words for lion, 4:7 answered by Gregory and Henry (Abel), and the vision question (Trapp's survey, Mercer and Henry: true content misapplied; Job 9:2; 42:7; Derek Thomas paraphrased). John 8:12-20 covered the treasury in the Court of the Women where the Booths lamps stood (Gill, Sproul, the Mishnah paraphrased), Isaiah 9, Chrysostom 'Not of Galilee', Augustine against the Manichees, Calvin's lightning, 5:31 versus 8:14 (Calvin: concession), two witnesses, and Sproul's 'It terrifies me'. 2 Peter 2:10-16 covered authadeis with Augustine's 'self-pleasers', the glorious ones (Calvin's magistrates versus the angelic reading with Jude 9; host leaned angelic), spiloi kai momoi against 1 Peter 1:19, deleazo as a fisherman's word, hearts trained in greed, and Balaam (Henry 'as Judas among the apostles'; Calvin on the donkey seeing first). Closing connections: prophets for wages (Ezekiel 13:19 and 2 Peter 2:15), and God's verdict on Job in Ezekiel 14:14 against Eliphaz's in Job 4:7, with John 8:15 'you judge according to the flesh'.
threads: Ezekiel 16 is next: the foundling bride (16:1-14), the harlotry (15-34), the judgment and the sisters Samaria and Sodom (35-58), and the everlasting covenant and atonement (59-63). It is the longest chapter in Ezekiel; teach it soberly. Chapter 15's vine leads into 17's eagles and vine. Keep tracking the glory arc (left to the Mount of Olives at 11:23; returns by the east gate in 43:1-5; the Ligonier 'Light of the World' devotional cross-references 43:1-3 with John 8:12) and the muteness (3:26 until 33:22). Calvin's Ezekiel lectures (calcom23 on CCEL) continue through chapter 20; Henry and Keil on Bible Hub.

Unused Ezekiel 13-15 material: Calvin's 'fleas' line on contending even with small opponents (13:17-18), 'false prophets were always immoderately fond of outward signs', 'no one can seriously reverence God unless he who feels him to be easily entreated' (13:22), 'God has erected the seat of his empire in our hearts' (14:3), the dogs that bite the stone (14:21), and 'excelled in privileges, but not in nature' (15); Henry's 'Those are the most dangerous seducers who suggest to sinners that which tends to lessen their dread of sin', 'for whom he sends he either finds fit or makes fit', 'It is ill with those people who can better hear pleasing lies than unpleasing truths', and 'not to lessen the useful good men of our own day by over-magnifying the ancients'; Poole's 'kennel of lesser cheats'; Spurgeon 816's 'volunteer band of ready assistants' and 'I would not give a farthing for your religion if you have never doubted about it'; Spurgeon 1651's 'He is the John of the Old Testament'; Gregory's 'turned his back in keeping silence' (13:5); Augustine's three classes of the saved (Noah, Daniel, Job); Chrysostom, Cyprian and Salvian on 14:14 on the SermonIndex fathers page.

Job 5 is next: Eliphaz finishes his first speech, 'man is born to trouble as the sparks fly upward' (5:7), 'he catches the wise in their own craftiness' (5:13, quoted by Paul in 1 Corinthians 3:19, the only New Testament quotation of the friends), and 'blessed is the one whom God reproves' (5:17). Ask how Paul can quote a speaker God rebukes in 42:7. Unused Job 4: Trapp's 'penal and probational' afflictions and Peter Martyr's 'before the fifth act', Henry's 'Those that pass rash and uncharitable censures ... do Satan's work' and 'A man's character is not to be taken from a single act', Gregory on heretics claiming a 'secret word'. Gregory's Moralia Book V is at lectionarycentral.com/GregoryMoralia/Book05.html (Windows-1252 encoded).

John 8:21-30 is next: 'I am going away ... you will die in your sin', 'You are from below; I am from above', 'unless you believe that I am he' (ego eimi), and 'When you have lifted up the Son of Man' (8:28, tie to 3:14 and 12:32). Unused 8:12-20 material: Augustine's Tractate 34 on the Light by whom the sun was made (quoted as paraphrase only today) and Tractate 35 'the light bears witness to itself'; Chrysostom's 'not from the weakness of the light, but from their own perverse will'; Ryle's 'False lights on every side' and 'Let us begin by following'; Sproul's 'God said it. That settles it.'; Gill on the rabbis calling Moses 'the light of the world'.

2 Peter 2:17-22 is next and closes the chapter: waterless springs and mists, 'promise them freedom, but they themselves are slaves of corruption', 'better never to have known the way of righteousness', and the dog and the sow (2:22; Proverbs 26:11). This raises the perseverance question again (link to 2:1 and Westminster Confession 17). Unused 2:10-16 material: Calvin on the donkey as Balaam's 'teacher' and 'Let there be then a stability of faith'; Trapp quoting Joseph Hall's 'There is no mouth into which God cannot put words'; Henry's 'Those who will not yield to usual methods of reproof will be but little influenced by miraculous appearances'; Gill on Bosor as Beor in a Chaldean accent; Bede on the donkey rebuking clerics (paraphrase only).

Voices quoted this episode: Calvin (Ezekiel 1; John 2 short), Spurgeon (Nos. 816 and 1651), Trapp (2), Gregory the Great (Pastoral Rule; Moralia), Henry (3), Chrysostom, Sproul, Augustine. Paraphrased: Poole, Keil and Delitzsch, Jerome, Augustine, Criswell, Derek Thomas, Gill, the Mishnah, Westminster Confession 5.4. Desiring God still returns 403 (no Piper); StudyLight blocks automated fetches, but SermonIndex carries Trapp and a church-fathers catena by verse (sermonindex.net/commentary/trapp/EZK/13, /ecf/JOB/4). Next time consider Boston, Owen, Bunyan, Sibbes, Ryle, Bede, and MacArthur or Schreiner on 2 Peter 2:17-22.

episodes.title: In Your Blood, Live: Ezekiel 16, Job 5, John 8, 2 Peter 2
episodes.summary: Ezekiel 16 was taught as an undated oracle inside the 592-591 B.C. block (8:1 to 20:1), growing the 'acted faithlessly' of 15:8 into a five-scene story: foundling, harlot, sentence, sisters, everlasting covenant. The chapter's reception came first: Rabbi Eliezer's ruling against using it as a synagogue reading (Mishnah Megillah 4:10, paraphrased) and Spurgeon's 1876 'A very extraordinary chapter' opening, so that the chapter is read as a mirror. Key points were Amorite and Hittite as moral pedigree (Calvin paraphrased), infant exposure, chayi 'Live!' twice (Poole quoted, 'the only eye that pitied'; Calvin paraphrased on Egypt and the doubling), Ruth 3:9 and Sinai (Calvin quoted on God swearing), 'But you trusted in your beauty' (Trapp's borrowed axe head), zanah and 'my' gifts turned to idols, Molech (Keil), the alliances with Egypt, Assyria and Chaldea as adultery (Calvin), and the inversion of a harlot who pays (hephek). The sentence was covered with Ligonier's 'His answer is often to give people over to it', and Sodom's guilt in 16:49-50 was read with Genesis 19 (Calvin and Chrysostom paraphrased). New Testament move one was Matthew 11:23-24, Capernaum and Sodom. The hard question, the restoration of Sodom (16:53), set Calvin's irony against Grotius's Moab and Ammon and Keil's real promise; the host leaned to a real promise of mercy to the nations because of 16:61. Covenant continuity was tied to Westminster Confession 7.6. Kipper in 16:63 got Spurgeon's 'pitch' (paraphrased), and New Testament move two was the cup of the new covenant. Calvin was quoted on hypocrites who want their sins buried, the closed mouth was linked to Ezekiel's own muteness, Spurgeon was quoted on 'sin and grace', and the application was to remember the field. Job 5 covered its three movements, bene reshef as 'children of the flame' (Keil paraphrased), and Gregory's Vulgate 'bird to flying' (quoted). The question of how Paul can quote Eliphaz (5:13 in 1 Corinthians 3:19) despite 42:7 was answered with Spurgeon No. 43 (quoted), Henry and Calvin paraphrased: inspiration records every speech accurately, and each sentence is tested by Scripture; 5:13 is true and the error is its target. 5:17-18 is true doctrine but the wrong diagnosis (Ligonier and Gregory paraphrased). John 8:21-30 covered the suicide jibe, below and above, singular sin and plural sins (Calvin), and ego eimi with Augustine quoted against Calvin's 'office not essence'; the host sided with Augustine because of 8:58. It also covered the 8:25 crux, the three lifting-up sayings with Sproul quoted ('darkest hour and greatest hour') and Chrysostom paraphrased, and Augustine on the Pentecost converts. 2 Peter 2:17-22 covered waterless springs (Calvin paraphrased), the targeting of new converts, and 2:19 with Calvin and Augustine's City of God 19.15 (quoted). The perseverance question was answered with Westminster Confession 17.1 (quoted), the 1689 agreement, Gill and Calvin paraphrased, the washed sow still a sow, and Calvin's 'gospel is a medicine' quoted. Closing connections: privilege raises the stakes (Jerusalem worse than Sodom; better never to have known), and Ezekiel's 'you shall know that I am the Lord' after mercy (16:62) echoed in John 8:28.
threads: Ezekiel 17-19 is next: the two eagles and the vine (17, the political version of chapter 16; Zedekiah's broken oath to Nebuchadnezzar, 17:15-19, links to 16:59 'despised the oath'), the cedar sprig planted on a high mountain (17:22-24, messianic), 'The soul who sins shall die' and the sour grapes proverb (18:2; Jeremiah 31:29), 'Why will you die, O house of Israel?' (18:31-32), and the lament for the princes, lioness and vine (19). Calvin's lectures continue through chapter 20 (calcom23 on CCEL). Chapter 23 will retell chapter 16 with Oholah and Oholibah. Keep tracking the glory arc (left at 11:23, returns 43:1-5) and the muteness (3:26 until 33:22), tied today to 16:63's closed mouth.

Unused Ezekiel 16 material: Henry's 'Those that in sincerity join themselves to the true God find enough in him for their satisfaction; and, though they still desire more of God, yet they never desire more than God', 'Every penny has God's image upon it as well as Caesar's', and his note that 'every transgression in the covenant does not throw us out of the covenant'. Trapp's 'like as in a house we cannot beat the dogs but the children will fall to crying' (16:60) and 'This fulness bred forgetfulness, and this saturity security' (16:49). Calvin's prayers at the end of Lectures 42 and 47, and his 'If, therefore, we wish our sins to be buried before God, we must remember them ourselves' (16:61). Spurgeon 1876's 'It takes a great deal to fill a man's mouth, and almost as much to shut it' and 'Thy very love confounds me as much as my sin does'. Gill on pacified (16:63). Spurgeon's Morning and Evening has an Ezekiel 16:6 entry, not yet fetched.

Job 6 is next: Job answers Eliphaz. Note the tafel link from episode 17: Job 6:6 asks whether tasteless food can be eaten without salt (tafel, the whitewash word of Ezekiel 13). Job's 'the arrows of the Almighty are in me' (6:4) and the friends as a deceitful wadi (6:15-20) answer Eliphaz's promises. Unused Job 5: Gregory 'they are only executing the will of God by the very way they are labouring to alter it' (5:13), Henry 'Actual transgressions are the sparks that fly out of the furnace of original corruption', Caryl via Henry 'he never makes a wound too great, too deep, for his own cure', and Spurgeon No. 43 quoting Caryl on 'Thou shalt come to thy grave' as willing death.

John 8:31-47 is next: 'to the Jews who had believed him' (picks up 8:30's 'many believed'), 'the truth will set you free', 'everyone who practices sin is a slave to sin' (8:34, which Augustine pairs with 2 Peter 2:19 in City of God 19.15, quoted today), children of Abraham, and 'You are of your father the devil'. Augustine's Tractates 40-42 and Chrysostom Homilies 54-55. Unused 8:21-30: Augustine 'You feed on earthly things... you have no heart for what is above', Ryle's 'Immorality slays its thousands, but unbelief its tens of thousands', Henry and Gill on ego eimi, Ligonier devotional 'How Not to Die in Sin'. Ego eimi culminates at 8:58.

2 Peter 3:1-9 is next: the second letter as reminder, scoffers in the last days, 'where is the promise of his coming?', the flood and the word, 'one day is as a thousand years', and 'not wishing that any should perish' (3:9). This answers the delay theme from episode 16 (Ezekiel 12:22 and 2 Peter 2:3). Unused 2:17-22: Leo the Great, Sermon 27 ('he has many whom he has bound still more tightly because they are suited for his designs'), Gill on the Hebrew word for sow meaning 'return', Henry 'licked up their own vomit', and the Ligonier devotionals 'Waterless Springs' and 'Slaves of Corruption'.

Voices quoted this episode: Spurgeon (1876 Ezekiel 16:62-63 sermon twice; No. 43 on Job 5:26), Poole, Calvin (Ezekiel 2, 2 Peter 1), Trapp, Ligonier devotional, Gregory the Great, Augustine (Tractate 38; City of God 19.15), Sproul (Ligonier sermon 'Jesus' Self-Witness'), Westminster Confession 17.1. Paraphrased: Keil, Henry, Gill, Chrysostom (Homily 6 on Matthew; Homily 53 on John), Mishnah Megillah 4:10, Calvin on 1 Corinthians and John, Westminster Confession 7.6. Desiring God still returns 403; no Piper found on these passages. Next time consider Owen, Watson, Boston, Brooks, Bunyan, Edwards on John 8:31-36, Lloyd-Jones on 2 Peter 3, and Caryl on Job 6.

episodes.title: Turn and Live: Ezekiel 17-19, Job 6, John 8, 2 Peter 3
episodes.summary: Ezekiel 17-19 was taught as the political retelling of chapter 16 inside the 592-591 B.C. block, hinged on 'despised the oath in breaking the covenant' (16:59; 17:18). Chapter 17's riddle (chidah and mashal) was decoded: Nebuchadnezzar, Jehoiachin carried to a 'city of merchants' (illustrated by the Babylonian ration tablets naming 'Ya'u-kinu, king of the land of Yahud'), Zedekiah as a low vine, Pharaoh as the second eagle; 17:19 'my oath' because Zedekiah swore by God (2 Chronicles 36:13; Calvin paraphrased as guardian of treaties, Psalm 15:4), and 17:16 was joined to 12:13 (die in Babylon without seeing it). The tender sprig (rak, 17:22) was read as Messianic in full and Zerubbabel in beginning (Calvin, Ellicott, Gill/Targum paraphrased), with Matthew 13:32 as the one New Testament move. Chapter 18 covered the sour-grapes proverb (Jeremiah 31:29; Lamentations 5:7), three generations, Henry quoted ('grace does not run in the blood'), Exodus 20:5 'of those who hate me' (Poole, Gill), Calvin on Adam, and Trapp's 'not falling into the water'; the hard question (18:31 'make yourselves a new heart' versus 11:19 and 36:26; 18:23, 32 versus election) was answered with Augustine's On Grace and Free Will 31 (quoted: he gives what he commands), Calvin (revealed will versus secret counsel; quoted, 'the character of a mourner'), Westminster Confession 10.1 paraphrased, Spurgeon No. 1795 (question, statement, oath; quoted 'Aversion to punishment is necessary to justice in a judge') and Sproul (quoted; same judge image). Chapter 19 was taught as a qinah: Jehoahaz to Egypt, Jehoiachin (Keil, against Gill's Jehoiakim) to Babylon, the vine burned by fire from its own branch (Zedekiah, Calvin) and 'no scepter', answered by 17:22 and previewing 21:27. Application: kill the sour-grapes proverb in your own mouth and ask for the heart God commands. Job 6 covered four movements, Shaddai's arrows, tafel tying back to Ezekiel 13's whitewash, Spurgeon No. 1730 quoted (salt and vinegar instead of oil and wine) with Henry's parallel, chesed in 6:14 and its textual question, the wadi and the caravans of Tema and Sheba, 6:21 'you see my calamity and are afraid', and Henry quoted ('God will out-do our hopes'). John 8:31-47 covered the 'believers' who did not continue (Chrysostom paraphrased; Ryle quoted on continuing), the truth as Christ (Chrysostom) versus the truth about Christ (Ryle), Chrysostom quoted on slaves of sin, Genesis 21 and the son in the house, Abraham's works, 8:41, and Augustine on the devil as murderer by a lie (paraphrased). 2 Peter 3:1-9 covered Peter's last letter as reminder (Calvin's rust paraphrased), the scoffers' uniformity argument linked to Ezekiel 12:22, word-water-fire, Irenaeus's world-week reading of 3:8 (quoted) against Spurgeon No. 447 (quoted), makrothumei, and the 'any' of 3:9 with Gill (paraphrased, the elect) against Calvin (quoted, revealed will); the host sided with Calvin. Closing connections: Ezekiel 18:23, 32 and 2 Peter 3:9 (delay as patience), and Ezekiel 18 with John 8:39 (lineage neither saves nor damns).
threads: Ezekiel 20-21 is next: a new date (20:1, August 591 B.C., the seventh year), elders inquiring again, the history of Israel's rebellion in Egypt, the wilderness and the land ('for the sake of my name', 20:9, 14, 22, 44), the 'statutes that were not good' crux (20:25), the forest fire of the Negeb and 'Is he not a maker of parables?' (20:45-49; ESV 21:1-5 numbering differs), the Song of the Sword (21), Nebuchadnezzar at the crossroads divining with arrows and liver (21:21), and 'until he comes whose right it is' (21:27; Genesis 49:10), promised today as the answer to 19:14 'no scepter'. Luke 23:31 'green wood/dry' is cross-referenced to 17:24 and 20:47. Keep tracking the glory arc (left at 11:23, returns 43:1-5) and Ezekiel's muteness (3:26 until 33:22). Calvin's Ezekiel lectures (calcom23 on CCEL) end at chapter 20.

Unused Ezekiel 17-19 material: Calvin 'truly men cannot absolve themselves without condemning God' (18:3) and his prayers; Calvin warning that Christian writers make themselves 'ridiculous to the Jews' by forcing every restoration text onto Christ (17:22); Henry 'though we are tied to give our children a good education he is not tied to bless it', 'Note, The reason why sinners die is because they will die', 'the way of sin is down-hill', and 'Ministers, when they boldly foretel, must yet bitterly lament the destruction of sinners' (19); Henry quoting Augustine's Latin 'Deus non jubet impossibilia'; Spurgeon 1795 'The sin must die or the sinner must die' and his 'turn or burn'; Sproul's 'God will never negotiate His righteousness'; Trapp 'Consideration necessarily precedeth conversion' and 'every tub shall stand upon its own bottom'; Augustine 'God commands some things which we cannot do, in order that we may know what we ought to ask of Him'; Lachish ostracon 3 (Coniah son of Elnathan gone down to Egypt) for the Egypt policy; Hamutal as mother of both Jehoahaz and Zedekiah.

Job 7 is next: Job turns from the friends to God ('Has not man a hard service on earth?', 7:1; 'my days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle', 7:6; 'Am I the sea, or a sea monster, that you set a guard over me?', 7:12; 'What is man, that you make so much of him?', 7:17, a dark parody of Psalm 8). Unused Job 6: Spurgeon No. 1471 on 6:10 ('They were bread and meat to him, though brought in a raven's mouth'), Gregory's Vulgate 'my sins' in 6:2 and the Mediator as the balance ('in the one scale He hung our woe in His own Person'), Gregory on 6:16 'Over those that fear the frost, the snow rushes down', Trapp on 6:14 'Heb. melted' and 6:25 Caryl on 'forcible' words, Ellicott seeing the Guadalquivir dry at Cordova in August.

John 8:48-59 is next: 'Are we not right in saying that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?', 'If anyone keeps my word, he will never see death', 'Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see my day', and 'before Abraham was, I am' (8:58), the culmination of ego eimi from 8:24 and 8:28 (episode 18 sided with Augustine against Calvin's 'office not essence' on 8:24). Unused 8:31-47: Ryle 'To know that we are being led captive, is the very first step toward deliverance', Spurgeon No. 2584 'You had the Lamp of life, but you made a dark lantern of it', No. 565 'The Great Liberator' (8:36), No. 492 'Nominal Christians, Real Infidels' (8:46), No. 2560 on 8:38 'Universal Fatherhood, A Lie', No. 1257 on 8:42; Augustine Tractate 42 quote on the murderer 'not as armed with a sword'.

2 Peter 3:10-18 is next and ends the letter: the day of the Lord as a thief, the elements dissolved with fire, 'what sort of people ought you to be', 'hastening the coming of the day of God' (3:12), new heavens and new earth, 'count the patience of our Lord as salvation' (3:15, which closes the 3:9 question), Paul's letters 'hard to understand' and twisted 'as they do the other Scriptures' (3:16, a key text for the canon), and 'grow in the grace and knowledge'. Calvin on 3:10 'two very different evils, too much haste, and slothfulness' is unused; also Calvin 'He is tardy who allows an occasion to pass by through slothfulness' and Spurgeon No. 447 'impatience may ripen into unbelief'.

Voices quoted this episode: Henry (2), Trapp, Augustine (On Grace and Free Will), Calvin (Ezekiel; 2 Peter), Spurgeon (Nos. 1795, 1730, 447), Sproul (Ligonier 'No Delight in the Death of the Wicked'), Ryle, Chrysostom (Homily 54 on John), Irenaeus (Against Heresies 5.28.3). episodes.title: For the Sake of My Name: Ezekiel 20-21, Job 7, John 8, 2 Peter 3
episodes.summary: Ezekiel 20-21 was taught from the 591 B.C. date (20:1, the tenth of Ab, eleven months and five days after 8:1 per Ellicott; Gill noting the same day the temple later burned, Jeremiah 52:12), with the elders' plan exposed in 20:32 ('Let us be like the nations', Calvin paraphrased). Chapter 20's history was laid out as three rounds (Egypt, wilderness, children) of grace, rebellion, wrath intended, and 'I acted for the sake of my name' (9, 14, 22, 44), with 'I lifted my hand' as the oath gesture and Calvin quoted that God's glory and the church's salvation are 'almost inseparably united'. The hard question, 'statutes that were not good' (20:25), set Justin Martyr (quoted, Dialogue 21) and Irenaeus (paraphrased, Against Heresies 4.15.1) reading it as the ceremonial law against Calvin (quoted, 'an immense heap of errors'), Keil and Poole; the host sided with Calvin and Keil via 20:26 and Romans 1:24 (first NT move), while granting the fathers that God can give a hard people what they demand. 20:33 got Henry's 'golden sceptre or the iron rod' (quoted); 20:37's rod and bond set Calvin (judgment roll-call, paraphrased) against Spurgeon No. 1840 (quoted, 'that which God counts He values'), resolved by 20:38; 20:43 shame after acceptance (Calvin paraphrased). Ezekiel 21 covered the forest fire and 'maker of parables', the sword against righteous and wicked (Henry quoted, 'God's graces and comforts make a great difference when his providence seems to make none'), the Song of the Sword, Nebuchadnezzar's crossroads divination with the British Museum liver model (Science Museum description), and 21:25-27, the crown removed 'until he comes, the one to whom judgment belongs', read with Keil on Genesis 49:10 and a Ligonier devotional (quoted), answering 19:14's 'no scepter', with Luke 1:32 as the second NT move. Application: refuse the plan to become like the nations; God's refusal to let you go is mercy. Job 7 covered Job turning from friends to God, hard service, the shuttle and tiqvah (hope/cord, Joshua 2), Gregory quoted ('we go on even in sleeping'), the sea and tannin, Spurgeon No. 2206 quoted ('The weaknesses of the saints lie near their strength'), 7:17 as a parody of Psalm 8 (Keil), notser ha'adam 'watcher of mankind', and Spurgeon No. 2705 paraphrased (Job was being honored, not punished); application: take the complaint to God. John 8:48-59 covered the Samaritan charge (Augustine: Samaritan means keeper, paraphrased), Chrysostom quoted on avenging insults to God but overlooking those to ourselves, 'never see death' with Spurgeon No. 2169 (after William Olney's death), the Father glorifying the Son, Abraham's joy (Augustine; Chrysostom's Moriah reading), and 8:58 with Augustine quoted ('was made' versus 'am') and Calvin quoted on 'a remarkable testimony of his Divine essence', closing episode 18's office-versus-essence thread; Jesus leaving the temple echoed the glory's departure in Ezekiel 10-11. 2 Peter 3:10-18 finished the letter: the thief, 'exposed' (Greek found), Calvin quoted on the two evils of haste and slothfulness, renewal not annihilation (Augustine City of God 20.16 and Calvin paraphrased), plural holinesses and godlinesses with David Strain (PCA) quoted, hastening as making the time fly, 3:15 closing the 3:9 patience question, 3:16 Paul's letters with 'the other Scriptures' (canon; Calvin on teachable reading), growth as the way to stand (Calvin; Spurgeon No. 2700's spinning top, paraphrased), and the doxology to Christ as proof of his deity (Calvin). Closing connections: the divine name (Ezekiel 20's 'for my name's sake' and 'I am the Lord', John 8:58, 2 Peter 3:18) and the God who watches and counts (Job 7:17-20 and Ezekiel 20:37).
threads: Ezekiel 22-23 is next: the bloody city indictment (22, with the dross in the furnace, 22:17-22, and 'I sought for a man... to stand in the breach', 22:30) and Oholah and Oholibah (23), which retells chapter 16 with Samaria and Jerusalem as two sisters and adds the Assyrian and Babylonian lovers; link 23 back to episode 18's chapter 16 and to the alliances. Ezekiel 24:1 dates the siege's start (January 588 B.C.) and Ezekiel's wife dies (24:15-18). Keep tracking the glory arc (left at 11:23, returns 43:1-5) and Ezekiel's muteness (3:26 until 33:22). Calvin's Ezekiel lectures end at chapter 20, so from chapter 21 on use Henry, Poole, Gill, Keil, Ellicott, Pulpit, Spurgeon, and Ligonier devotionals; Trapp on StudyLight is behind a bot wall.

Unused Ezekiel 20-21 material: Calvin 'This then is the fruit of penitence, this is true humility, flowing from genuine shame' (20:43) and on 20:44 'his glory extends farther than his pity'; Calvin on shebet as 'a shepherd's crook' (20:37); Keil on 20:25 'The ceremonial commandments given by God were good' and on mishpat in 21:27 as 'right in an objective sense, as belonging to God'; Poole 'the not good is very bad, inconvenient, and hurtful'; Gill on 20:25 listing views and Abendana reading 21:27 of Messiah; Henry on 21:22 'What services God designs men for he will be sure in his providence to lead them to' and 21:27 'Christ has an incontestable title to the dominion'; Spurgeon No. 688 'Sweet Savor' on 20:41 (fetched, not mined); Irenaeus Against Heresies 4.15.1 'a state of servitude suited to their wish'.

Job 8 is next: Bildad's first speech ('Does God pervert justice?', 8:3; 'Your children have sinned', 8:4; 'though your beginning was small, your latter days will be very great', 8:7; the papyrus and the spider's web, 8:11-15). Spurgeon No. 311 (Job 8:7) and No. 651 'A Sermon from a Rush' (8:11-13) are in the Spurgeon Gems index; Henry on Job 7:6 already pointed to 8:14 ('Many weave the spider's web'). Unused Job 7: Henry 'While we are living, as we are sowing, so we are weaving. Every day, like the shuttle, leaves a thread behind it'; Gregory 'to the web there is a delay of growth, but to the present life there is no delay of coming to an end' and on 7:17; Spurgeon No. 2705 'You may be patient under suffering, but not patient under sin'; Spurgeon No. 1258 on Job 7:1 (fetched, not mined).

John 9:1-12 is next: the man born blind, 'who sinned, this man or his parents?' (9:2, which ties to the Job friends' theology and to Ezekiel 18), 'that the works of God might be displayed in him', 'I am the light of the world' again (9:5, back to 8:12), the mud and the pool of Siloam ('Sent'). Augustine Tractate 44 and Chrysostom Homilies 56-57. Unused John 8:48-59: Spurgeon No. 2652 'Let this stand as the very crown jewel among all the gems that make up Abraham's crown'; Spurgeon No. 2169 'If the believer shall never see death, then the unbeliever shall never see life'; Begg (Truth For Life) 'Divinity has no past'; Chrysostom on 'my day' as the crucifixion foreshown in the ram and Isaac (paraphrased today).

1 John begins next (1:1-4): give the book its introduction (the apostle John, late first century, Ephesus by tradition; tests of life; 'that which we have seen and touched' answering early docetism), and connect 1 John 1:1 to John 1:1. Unused 2 Peter 3:10-18: Calvin 'we are not forbidden to read Paul's Epistles' (3:16) and 'This is a remarkable passage to prove the divinity of Christ' (3:18); Henry 'By how much the stronger grace is in us, by so much the more stedfast shall we be in the truth'; Spurgeon No. 1125 'MEN have frequently inferred liberty to sin from the apparent absence of God from the world'; Spurgeon No. 1997 on 3:15; Strain's 'homesick for heaven'.

Voices quoted this episode: Calvin (Ezekiel 20:9, 20:25; John 8:58; 2 Peter 3:10), Justin Martyr (Dialogue 21), Matthew Henry (Ezekiel 20:33; 21:3), Spurgeon (Nos. 1840, 2206), Ligonier devotional 'The Messiah's Kingdom', Gregory the Great (Moralia 8), Chrysostom (Homily 55 on John), Augustine (Tractate 43), David Strain (FPC Jackson, 'Hastening the Day'). Paraphrased: Irenaeus, Keil, Poole, Gill, Ellicott, Augustine (Tractate 43 on Samaritan; City of God 20.16), Spurgeon (Nos. 2705, 2169, 2700). Desiring God still blocks automated fetches (no Piper); Ligonier's Sproul sermons on these passages are video only. Next time try Owen or Boston, Kidner or Ash on Job 8, Ryle (archive.org) on John 9, and Candlish or Lloyd-Jones on 1 John.

episodes.title: No Man in the Breach: Ezekiel 22-23, Job 8, John 9, 1 John 1
episodes.summary: Ezekiel 22-23 was taught as undated oracles between 20:1 (591 B.C.) and 24:1 (January 588 B.C.), explaining the sword of chapter 21. Chapter 22: ir haddamim, 'city of bloods', borrowed from Nahum 3:1's title for Nineveh; Keil's three groups marked by 'to shed blood' (22:6, 9, 12); 'me you have forgotten' (22:12, Henry paraphrased); the dross (sig) and furnace with Gregory the Great's Pastoral Rule quoted on the metals (brass as murmuring under blows, tin as pretense, iron as malice, lead as earthbound desire) against Henry's brazen-face reading, and Henry quoted that God sits by his own in the furnace but leaves dross there; then all classes (22:23-29, whitewash callback to 13:10). The hard question, 'I found none' (22:30, gader and perets) while Jeremiah was in Jerusalem, was answered with Gill (not among these classes), Ellicott (none of commanding standing), Jeremiah 11:14 and 15:1 and Ezekiel 14:14 (intercession closed), and D. A. Carson quoted ('Theirs was not the task of rebuilding the wall'), then Isaiah 59:16 and 1 Timothy 2:5 as New Testament move one. Chapter 23: Oholah 'her tent' and Oholibah 'my tent is in her' (Keil quoted, Poole paraphrased), differing from chapter 16 by focusing on guilt and the alliances (Keil); Samaria and Assyria (722 B.C.), Oholibah 'saw this' and grew worse (Henry quoted, 'made worse by that which should make them better'), the vermilion wall pictures with Keil on Assyrian palace reliefs and Layard's Lachish reliefs, lovers turned executioners, Carson quoted on the language ('meant to be horrible') and the metaphor not walking on all fours, the sister's cup (23:31-34) with Gethsemane as New Testament move two, and Molech and temple 'on the same day' (23:38-39). Application: what have you watched destroy someone else that you are walking toward? Job 8: Bildad the Shuhite (Shuah, Genesis 25:2, via Henry), four parts, 8:3-4 and 'your children have sinned', Henry quoted ('extraordinary afflictions ... the trial of extraordinary graces') and paraphrased (advocate for God turned accuser), the appeal to tradition, gome papyrus (Exodus 2:3), spider's house, Gregory's Moralia quoted ('words of wondrous truth ... running himself through') and paraphrased (watering the river while gardens dry), Spurgeon No. 651 quoted on self-examination, and No. 311 paraphrased that 8:7 came true in Job 42. John 9:1-12: Chrysostom on Jesus seeing first, Sproul quoted ('Had they not read the book of Job'), Chrysostom using Ezekiel 18 against inherited punishment, Augustine and Chrysostom that sin was not the cause, Spurgeon No. 2309 quoted on Job's friends, Chrysostom quoted on clay and Genesis 2, Siloam ('Sent', Hezekiah's pool, the 2004 discovery, callback to the Booths water-drawing), 'I am the man', and Ryle paraphrased on not measuring others' experience by our own. 1 John began with an introduction (apostle John, Ephesus, late first century; Irenaeus on John until Trajan; docetism; Cerinthus and the bath-house story quoted), the one long sentence of 1:1-3, the link to John 1:1-4, the verbs heard, seen, looked upon, touched (Luke 24:39), Augustine quoted ('Because he touched the Man, he confessed the God') and paraphrased (witness as martyr), koinonia and joy, and Spurgeon No. 409 paraphrased ('is', not 'was'). Closing connections: Bildad's theology and the disciples' question answered by Jesus (Sproul), and the man in the breach: Ezekiel 22:30 found none, Ezekiel 14:14 named Job, and Job 42:8 has Job praying for Bildad.
threads: Ezekiel 24-26 is next: the date of the siege's start (24:1-2, tenth day of the tenth month of the ninth year, January 588 B.C., written down 'this very day'), the parable of the rusted cooking pot (24:3-14; Gregory's Pastoral Rule already quotes 24:12 'her exceeding rust went not out from her, not even by fire', unused), the death of Ezekiel's wife, 'the delight of your eyes', and his command not to mourn (24:15-27), the promise that his mouth will be opened when the fugitive arrives (24:27, toward 33:22), and the turn to the nations: Ammon, Moab, Edom, Philistia (25) and Tyre (26). Spurgeon No. 2286 'An Ancient Question Modernized' is on Ezekiel 24:19 (Spurgeon Gems index). Keep tracking the glory arc (left at 11:23, returns 43:1-5).

Unused Ezekiel 22-23 material: Henry 'he smites his hand against the sin before he lays his hand upon the sinner' (22:13), 'Sin makes a gap in the hedge of protection that is about a people' (22:30), 'Note, Sin alienates God's mind from the sinner, and justly, for it is the alienation of the sinner's mind from God' (23:18), 'Men need no more to sink them than the weight of their own sins' (23:35); Carson's 'There is no fidelity without remembering' and 'You cannot just flirt with sin' (TGC sermon on Ezekiel 16 and 23); Pulpit 'there is hope, as well as terror, in the parable' (22:18); JFB on Jeremiah forbidden to pray (Jeremiah 11:14); Biblical Illustrator's Spurgeon quoting Manton on 23:13 ('We easily catch an infectious disease from one another, but no man receiveth health from another's company'); Keil's preference for reading 22:25 as 'princes' (nesi'eha) with the Septuagint; Ellicott that in Egypt adultery was punished by cutting off nose and ears (23:25).

Job 9:1-20 is next: Job answers Bildad, 'how can a man be in the right before God?' (9:2), the God who removes mountains and commands the sun, 'he passes by me, and I see him not' (9:11), and 'Though I am in the right, I cannot answer him' (9:15), leading toward the cry for an arbiter in 9:33. Unused Job 8: Gregory 'For he desires not to be holy, but to be called holy' (8:12) and the spider's web as works blown away by 'the breath of man's regard'; Henry's bee versus spider (8:14) and 'God was pleased to join issue with him' (8:7); Spurgeon No. 311 'Evil things begin as mountains, they end as molehills'.

John 9:13-25 is next: the Pharisees interrogate the healed man, the Sabbath charge, the parents afraid of being put out of the synagogue (9:22), and 'One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see' (9:25). Unused John 9:1-12: Calvin's three errors in judging affliction, including 'If my brother meets with adversity, I instantly acknowledge the judgment of God; but if God chastises me with a heavier stroke, I wink at my sins'; Augustine Tractate 44 'He spat on the ground, He made clay of His spittle; for the Word was made flesh' and the anointed-then-washed catechumen reading; Chrysostom 'sin alone is an evil, but blindness is not an evil'; Ryle 'Opportunities once lost can never be retrieved'; Spurgeon No. 2309 'sacred excavators' (paraphrased today), No. 1754 and No. 1977 (fetched, not mined), No. 2950 on 9:11.

1 John 1:5-10 is next: 'God is light, and in him is no darkness at all', walking in the light, fellowship with one another, the blood of Jesus cleansing, 'If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves', and 'If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive' (1:9). Augustine's Homily 1 on 1 John (newadvent 170201) continues into those verses. Unused 1 John 1:1-4: Augustine 'Those saw, we have not seen, and yet we are fellows; because we hold the faith in common'; Spurgeon No. 409 'though he knew Him no more after the flesh, yet he knew Him after a nobler sort'; Irenaeus 1.26.1 on Cerinthus ('Christ departed from Jesus'); Ellicott on Polycarp's echo of 1 John 4:2-3. Spurgeon Nos. 3272 and 3406 are on 1 John 1:4.

Voices quoted this episode: Gregory the Great (Pastoral Rule 3, Ezekiel 22:18; Moralia 8, Job 8:11-13), Matthew Henry (Ezekiel 22:20; 23:11; Job 8:4), D. A. Carson (For the Love of God vol. 2, September 19; TGC sermon 'Whoredom Part 6'), Keil (Ezekiel 23:4), Spurgeon (Nos. 651, 2309), R. C. Sproul (Ligonier 'Suffering and the Glory of God'), Chrysostom (Homily 56 on John), Irenaeus (Against Heresies 3.3.4), Augustine (Homily 1 on 1 John). Paraphrased: Gill, Ellicott, Poole, JFB, Ryle, Spurgeon Nos. 311 and 409, Augustine Tractate 44. Calvin was rested (his Ezekiel lectures end at chapter 20). Desiring God and Monergism still return 403 to automated fetches. Gospel Translations hosts Carson's For the Love of God by date (use gospeltranslations.org, not en.gospeltranslations.org, if one errors). Next time consider Owen, Boston, Candlish or Lloyd-Jones on 1 John 1:5-10, and Caryl on Job 9.

episodes.title: The Delight of Your Eyes: Ezekiel 24-26, Job 9, John 9, 1 John 1
episodes.summary: Ezekiel 24-26 was taught from the dated start of the siege (24:1-2, January 588 B.C., 2 Kings 25:1, later the fast of Zechariah 8:19; Ellicott on same-day knowledge, Henry on the date confirming the prophet). The pot parable answered the 11:3 cauldron slogan; chel'ah 'corrosion/rust' found only here (Ellicott), blood left on bare rock, 'no lot', and Gregory the Great's Pastoral Rule quoted on 24:12 (rust not removed even by fire). The death of Ezekiel's wife centered on machmad eneykha, 'the delight of your eyes' (24:16, 21, 25), with Carson quoted twice ('massive restraint'; silent 'because of the command of God'), mourning customs and Ezekiel the priest as an exception (Keil, Ellicott); the hard question (why take her, why forbid grief) was answered with Poole (taken to God, paraphrased), Henry (the sign cost him dear, paraphrased; 'least safe which is most dear' quoted), Spurgeon No. 2286 quoted ('terrible lesson... terribly taught'), and Henry/Carson/Keil on the tearless people, the host siding with Keil via Leviticus 26:39-42; First Thessalonians 4:13 was NT move one. Application: what is the delight of your eyes, and could you lose it and still obey? 24:27 promised the opened mouth (to 33:21-22). Chapter 25's four oracles (Ammon's 'Aha', Moab's sneer, Edom's revenge, Philistia) were placed between siege and fall (Carson: seven nations, Babylon absent). Chapter 26's Tyre was taught as a commercial rival ('I shall be replenished'; Henry quoted on being pleased at others' fall), the island city, waves of nations, Josephus (Against Apion 1.21) on the thirteen-year siege, the 'he' to 'they' shift (Ellicott) and Alexander's 332 B.C. causeway from old Tyre's rubble (Poole); hard question 'never rebuilt' (26:14) answered with Gill (restriction; Jerome saw a noble Tyre), Ellicott (the Tyre that then was), and Acts 21:3-4 as NT move two; 26:20 tsevi. Job 9:1-20: Job agrees with Bildad (Henry on owning agreement), turns Eliphaz's 4:17 question into his own lawsuit (tsadaq, riv), Gregory's Moralia quoted ('put under God receives righteousness; being put with God he loses it'), the hymn, 9:8 and 9:11 linked to Mark 6:48, Rahab, and 9:20 with Spurgeon No. 2932 quoted (if any man could be justified by works, it was Job) against the Pulpit reading of a protest about power; 9:15's appeal for mercy as the right instinct. John 9:13-25: kneading among the Mishnah's thirty-nine works, Calvin on Christ choosing the Sabbath, schisma, the man's growing confession, Calvin quoted ('this boldness is another miracle'), the synagogue ban (Calvin on ancient excommunication; Augustine quoted 'They cast out, but Christ received'), 'Give glory to God' as Joshua 7:19 oath (Calvin; Augustine paraphrased 'deny what you have received'), Chrysostom quoted ('So strong is truth, so weak is falsehood') and Spurgeon No. 2955 paraphrased. 1 John 1:5-10: God is light (Calvin), three 'if we say' claims and two answers, fellowship with one another, present-tense cleansing (Calvin paraphrased), 1:8 versus 1:10 with Westminster Confession 6.5, Augustine quoted on light sins, homologeo, 'faithful and just' with Calvin (fidelity to promise; 'hell within us' quoted) against Spurgeon No. 255 (justice satisfied), and Sproul quoted on self-deception plus his 'sin of arrogance' story. Closing connections: Job 9:2 answered by 1 John 1:7-9, and Job 9:11 'he passes by me, and I see him not' against John 9:1 'as he passed by, he saw'.
threads: Ezekiel 27-28 is next: the lament over Tyre as a great ship (27, with its catalogue of trading partners) and the oracle against the prince/king of Tyre, 'you were in Eden, the garden of God' and the guardian cherub (28:12-19, the Satan-fall reading of the fathers versus the historical king), then Sidon (28:20-26) and the promise to gather Israel. Promised: Ezekiel 29:18 says Nebuchadnezzar and his army 'had no wages from Tyre' for the long siege; address it honestly when we reach it (Ellicott on Ezekiel 26 intro and 29:18). Keep tracking the muteness thread (3:26, promised end at 24:27, fulfilled 33:21-22) and the glory arc (left at 11:23, returns 43:1-5).

Unused Ezekiel 24-26 material: Henry 'Those who have the world in their hearts lament the loss of great men more than the loss of good men' (26:17); Henry 'their calamities have been their neighbours' entertainments' (25:3-6); Henry 'If this was done to the green tree, what shall be done to the dry?' (24:21, with Luke 23:31); Henry's suggestion that Ezekiel prayed for his wife and was not heard; Keil 'overwhelming grief, for which there were no tears' (24:23); Ligonier devotional 'God never finds Himself in a desperate situation'; Spurgeon No. 2286's Christological accommodation of 24:19 ('Wilt thou not tell us what these things are to us') to the passion; Ellicott on Tyre's colonies (Cyprus, Carthage, Cadiz) and Herodotus's pillars in the temple of Hercules (26:11); Henry on Edom and Judas Maccabeus (1 Maccabees 5:3) and Hyrcanus; the Tell el-Umeiri seal impression of an Ammonite king (Baalis?) for Jeremiah 40:14; Benson/Maundrell on fishermen drying nets at Tyre.

Job 9:21-35 is next: 'I regard not myself; I loathe my life', 'he destroys both the blameless and the wicked' (9:22), 'my days are swifter than a runner' and 'skiffs of reed' (9:25-26), 'If I wash myself with snow' (9:30-31; Spurgeon No. 1908 'Washed to Greater Foulness' and No. 3069), and 'There is no arbiter between us, who might lay his hand on us both' (9:33; Spurgeon No. 661 'The Great Arbitration Case', fetched, not mined), promised today as the someone who stands in the case. Unused Job 9:1-20: Gregory Moralia 9 on 9:11 'often that is the gift of grace which it takes to be wrath, and often that is the wrath of God's severity, which it supposes to be grace'; Gregory on Arcturus as the Church; Spurgeon No. 350 'self-righteousness is born with us' and the Cork epitaph ('he made heaven debtor to mercy'); Cambridge on kesil as a chained giant; JFB's Egyptian hieroglyph of a man walking on waves.

John 9:26-41 is next: 'Do you also want to become his disciples?', 'We are disciples of Moses', 'Never since the world began', 'You were born in utter sin', the man cast out, Jesus finding him ('Do you believe in the Son of Man?'), worship, and 'For judgment I came into this world, that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind' (9:39-41). Unused John 9:13-25: Calvin 'they act as if one were endeavoring to extinguish a strong flame by his breath' and on the Vespasian healing in Suetonius; Augustine Tractate 44 'kept the Sabbath carnally, and profaned it spiritually', 'herald of grace', and the anointed-but-not-yet-washed reading; Chrysostom Homily 58 'this is the nature of truth, by the very means by which it seems to be assailed by men, by these it becomes stronger'; Spurgeon No. 2955 'That man will never move the world who lets the world move him'; Spurgeon No. 1393 on 9:21 'Speak for Yourself' (fetched, not mined).

1 John 2:1-11 is next: 'that you may not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father' (parakletos), 'he is the propitiation (hilasmos) for our sins, and not for ours only but also for the sins of the whole world' (2:2, a Reformed exegetical crux; Calvin and Owen), 'whoever says I know him but does not keep his commandments is a liar', walking as he walked, and the old and new commandment. Promised today: 2:2 grounds why God is 'just' to forgive (closing the Calvin versus Spurgeon No. 255 tension). Unused 1 John 1:5-10: Augustine Homily 1 'Tell men what you are, tell God what you are', 'if you have confessed yourself a sinner, the truth is in you', and on 2:1 'fear not to lose your cause in your confession'; Calvin 'integrity of conscience is alone that which distinguishes light from darkness' (1:7); Westminster Confession 15.6 on private confession to God and to an offended brother; Spurgeon Nos. 223, 663, 1986 (1:7) and 1241 'Honest Dealing with God' (1:8-10, fetched, not mined).

Voices quoted this episode: Gregory the Great (Pastoral Rule 3.13 on Ezekiel 24:12; Moralia 9 on Job 9:2), D. A. Carson (For the Love of God vol. 2, September 21, twice), C. H. Spurgeon (Nos. 2286, 2932), Matthew Henry (Ezekiel 24:16; 26:2), John Calvin (John 9:17; 1 John 1:9), Augustine (Tractate 44 on John; Homily 1 on 1 John), John Chrysostom (Homily 58 on John), R. C. Sproul (Ultimately, 'God's Truth Is Trustworthy'). Paraphrased: Poole, Keil, Ellicott, Gill (citing Jerome), Josephus, Henry (Job 9), Pulpit Commentary, Spurgeon Nos. 350, 2955, 255, Westminster Confession 6.5, Mishnah Shabbat 7:2. Desiring God still returns 403 (no Piper). Henry's full commentary is fetchable at biblestudytools.com (matthew-henry-complete); Calvin's commentaries come as plain text from ccel.org/ccel/c/calvin/calcomNN/cache/calcomNN.txt (34 = John vol. 1, 45 = Catholic Epistles); Gregory's Moralia is at lectionarycentral.com/GregoryMoralia/BookNN.html. Next time try Owen or Flavel on 1 John 2:1-2, Caryl on Job 9:33, Ryle on John 9:39-41, and Keil or the fathers on Ezekiel 28:12-19.

episodes.description:
John 9:13-25, 1 John 1:5-10, Job 9:1-20, Ezekiel 24-26

The siege of Jerusalem begins, Ezekiel's wife, the delight of his eyes, dies, and he is told not to mourn, while Tyre gloats over Jerusalem's fall. Job asks how a man can be in the right before God, the man born blind faces the Pharisees with 'One thing I do know', and John tells us that God is light and faithful and just to forgive.
